deductions.conclusion: Nonzero pure thin-image phases have matrix degree at least 24 on SL2/2O and 36 on SL2/2I; a fixed bad marker has degree at most D-8 or D-12. At the endpoint the phase is cubic in a real minimum-degree seed.
deductions.new_step: Associated graded matrix-degree ring is a domain; normalized curve degrees convert exactly to matrix degrees.
deductions.boundary: Thin PHASE images only; no restriction on full-image failures or inference from thin auxiliary heights.

deductions.conclusion: Any nonzero pure Gaussian polynomial with one-dimensional real image in C has a fixed bad polynomial marker of degree at most deg(P)-1.
deductions.new_step: Adapt the curve-normalization proof to the Gaussian real locus; compactness is unnecessary for the finite-module argument.
deductions.boundary: No existence of such pure phases; excludes them in proved safe classes.

deductions.conclusion: Every map U x A^a -> T/F factors through r=1-SY for U=A2 minus {SY=1} and free finite torus quotient T/F.
deductions.new_step: All connected finite covers are cyclic r-root covers and have unit group C* times v^Z.
deductions.boundary: Over C; native surface exclusion already follows from log dimension. Virtually abelian targets in general are not classified.

deductions.conclusion: The full degree<=11 octahedral positive field theorem extends to arbitrary complex coefficient algebras, with ordinary cutoff stabilization and a common uncomputed integer slope.
deductions.boundary: No sharp nonreduced slope, new numeric bound, degree-12 field closure or all-degree MZ conclusion.

not_promoted: Critical Gorensteinness of an HC4 plinth does not follow from Gaussian nilpotent lifting.
Ordinary moment ideals cannot be replaced by their radicals over nonreduced coefficient algebras.
